strings.venues.glowmatic.name: Glowmatic

strings.venues.stoopStrengthGym.blurb: A basement gym with kettlebells, battle ropes and a chalk-dusted floor.
strings.venues.ninthHourCoffee.name: Ninth Hour Coffee
strings.venues.ninthHourCoffee.blurb: Pour-overs and oat lattes for the laptop crowd. Hiring baristas.
strings.venues.handMeUpThrift.name: Hand-Me-Up Thrift
strings.venues.handMeUpThrift.blurb: Racks of vintage tees, old band merch and one-off finds. Hiring retail staff.
strings.venues.brickwave.name: Brickwave
strings.venues.brickwave.blurb: A brick-walled club in Gowanus with a heavy sound system.
strings.venues.wallaboutFreight.name: Wallabout Freight Co-op
strings.venues.wallaboutFreight.blurb: A delivery co-op by the Navy Yard. Hiring riders.
strings.venues.owlHoursDeli.name: Owl Hours Deli
strings.venues.owlHoursDeli.blurb: Open all night on the Lower East Side. Coffee, sandwiches and snacks.
strings.venues.steamWindowDumplings.name: Steam Window Dumplings
strings.venues.steamWindowDumplings.blurb: Pork and chive dumplings, pan-fried or steamed.
strings.venues.stationUnionSq.name: Union Sq station
strings.venues.stationUnionSq.blurb: A busy underground hub on the 4, 5 and 6 lines under Union Square.
strings.venues.liftLaneFitness.name: Lift Lane Fitness
strings.venues.liftLaneFitness.blurb: Treadmills, rowers and a full rack of dumbbells in Chelsea.
strings.venues.overtimeEspresso.name: Overtime Espresso
strings.venues.overtimeEspresso.blurb: Espresso and cortados in the East Village. Hiring baristas.
strings.venues.sidecutStudio.name: Sidecut Studio
strings.venues.sidecutStudio.blurb: A small SoHo boutique stocking streetwear from local designers. Hiring retail staff.
strings.venues.afterglass.name: Afterglass
strings.venues.afterglass.blurb: A mirrored club near the Hudson with a late dance floor.
strings.venues.sixthFloorLabs.name: Sixth Floor Labs
strings.venues.sixthFloorLabs.blurb: A startup office near Madison Square. Hiring junior devs.
strings.landmarks.brooklynBridge.name: Brooklyn Bridge
strings.landmarks.brooklynBridge.info: A stone-towered suspension bridge from 1883 linking Manhattan and Brooklyn, with a walkway above the traffic.
strings.landmarks.manhattanBridge.name: Manhattan Bridge
strings.landmarks.manhattanBridge.info: A blue steel suspension bridge between Chinatown and DUMBO. Trains rumble across it all day.
strings.landmarks.queensboroBridge.name: Queensboro Bridge
strings.landmarks.queensboroBridge.info: A steel cantilever bridge that hops over Roosevelt Island from Midtown East to Queens.
strings.landmarks.wedgeBuilding.name: Fifth Ave wedge
strings.landmarks.wedgeBuilding.info: A narrow triangular tower from 1902 where Fifth Avenue and Broadway cross.
strings.landmarks.decoSpire.name: Lexington Deco spire
strings.landmarks.decoSpire.info: An Art Deco skyscraper whose stainless-steel crown shines over Midtown East at night.
strings.landmarks.statueOfLiberty.name: Statue of Liberty
strings.landmarks.statueOfLiberty.info: The copper statue in the harbor, seen from the waterfront railing at the Battery.
strings.landmarks.washingtonSquareArch.name: Washington Square Arch
strings.landmarks.washingtonSquareArch.info: A marble arch at the south end of Fifth Avenue, framing Washington Square Park.
strings.landmarks.centralPark.name: Central Park
strings.landmarks.centralPark.info: Lawns, lakes and winding paths in the middle of Manhattan.
strings.landmarks.highLine.name: High Line
strings.landmarks.highLine.info: A park built on an old elevated rail line above the West Side.
strings.landmarks.prospectPark.name: Prospect Park
strings.landmarks.prospectPark.info: Meadows, woods and a lake in the middle of Brooklyn.
strings.landmarks.flushingMeadows.name: Flushing Meadows Corona Park
strings.landmarks.flushingMeadows.info: Wide lawns around the Unisphere, the steel globe from the 1964 World's Fair.
strings.landmarks.astoriaPark.name: Astoria Park
strings.landmarks.astoriaPark.info: A riverside park with a public pool and views of two bridges.
strings.landmarks.queensBallpark.name: Queens ballpark
strings.landmarks.queensBallpark.info: The baseball stadium by Flushing Bay, loud on game nights.
strings.landmarks.brooklynArena.name: Brooklyn arena
strings.landmarks.brooklynArena.info: A rust-coloured arena over Atlantic Avenue for basketball and concerts.
strings.landmarks.cityHall.name: City Hall
strings.landmarks.cityHall.info: The seat of New York City government, in a park in Lower Manhattan.
strings.landmarks.brooklynBoroughHall.name: Brooklyn Borough Hall
strings.landmarks.brooklynBoroughHall.info: The Greek Revival home of the Brooklyn Borough President, by Cadman Plaza.
strings.landmarks.queensBoroughHall.name: Queens Borough Hall
strings.landmarks.queensBoroughHall.info: The Queens Borough President's office, on Queens Boulevard in Kew Gardens.
strings.landmarks.midtownTerminal.name: 42nd St terminal
strings.landmarks.midtownTerminal.info: A Beaux-Arts rail terminal with a starry ceiling over its main hall.
strings.landmarks.pennStation.name: Penn Station
strings.landmarks.pennStation.info: A busy rail station under the West Side of Midtown.
strings.landmarks.jamaicaStation.name: Jamaica Station
strings.landmarks.jamaicaStation.info: A rail hub in Jamaica where commuter trains meet the airport train.
strings.landmarks.timesSquare.name: Times Square
strings.landmarks.timesSquare.info: Giant screens, crowds and street performers at the crossroads of Midtown.
strings.landmarks.dumbo.name: DUMBO
strings.landmarks.dumbo.info: Cobblestones and warehouses tucked between the Brooklyn and Manhattan bridges.
strings.landmarks.coneyIslandBoardwalk.name: Coney Island Boardwalk
strings.landmarks.coneyIslandBoardwalk.info: A wooden boardwalk along the beach, with rides and food stands on the other side.
strings.landmarks.flushingMainStreet.name: Flushing Main Street
strings.landmarks.flushingMainStreet.info: Bakeries, dumpling stalls and crowded sidewalks around the Main St stop.
strings.landmarks.september11Memorial.name: 9/11 Memorial
strings.landmarks.september11Memorial.info: Two reflecting pools mark where the Twin Towers stood. The names of the nearly 3,000 people killed on September 11, 2001, and in the 1993 bombing are inscribed around them.
strings.landmarks.bronxBallpark.name: Bronx ballpark
strings.landmarks.bronxBallpark.info: The baseball stadium in the South Bronx, a short walk from the Grand Concourse.
strings.landmarks.statenIslandFerry.name: Staten Island Ferry
strings.landmarks.statenIslandFerry.info: The orange ferry between St. George and Lower Manhattan, free to ride.
